findings.title: Mutable default list shares customer IDs across requests
findings.evidence:
def record_customer(customer_id, customer_ids=[]):
    """Return IDs belonging only to this independent request."""
    customer_ids.append(customer_id)
    return customer_ids
findings.explanation: The mutable default argument is created once and reused. Calling record_customer(1) followed by record_customer(2) without explicit lists returns [1, 2] on the second call, violating request isolation. The second call also mutates the list returned by the first call.
findings.recommendation: Use customer_ids=None and create a new list inside the function when the argument is None.
findings.suggested_test: Call record_customer(1) and then record_customer(2) without explicit lists. Assert the results are [1] and [2], respectively, and are distinct objects.

findings.title: Mutable default shares customer IDs across independent requests
findings.evidence:
def record_customer(customer_id, customer_ids=[]):
    """Return IDs belonging only to this independent request."""
    customer_ids.append(customer_id)
    return customer_ids
findings.explanation: The default list is created once and reused by every call that omits customer_ids. Later requests receive earlier customer IDs, violating the documented isolation. Subsequent calls also mutate lists returned by earlier calls.
findings.recommendation: Default customer_ids to None and create a new list inside the function when it is None.
findings.suggested_test: Call first = record_customer('A'), then second = record_customer('B') without passing lists. Assert first == ['A'], second == ['B'], and first is not second.
